walkthroughs.body_html: Strengths: case studies like HM support separate stores; clear and testable. Weaknesses: too simple — LTM has subtypes (episodic, semantic, procedural); rehearsal alone does not always create LTM (deep processing matters too).

Loftus showed leading questions distort recall. Participants who heard cars smashed rather than hit remembered higher speeds and broken glass. This shows reconstructive memory has real-world consequences for justice.
The Ponzo illusion uses depth cues — the brain assumes the upper line is further away, so it must be bigger. The Müller-Lyer uses fins. These illusions support Gregory's constructivist theory.
